expertInsight: System Architect is awarded after you earn four credentials: Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect. There is no separate System Architect exam. Platform Developer I also counts toward Application Architect, so three credentials in this path are additional if you already hold Application Architect.

personas.label: Enterprise solution architects
personas.description: You plan how Salesforce connects to company systems, identity providers, and release processes.

personas.label: Integration specialists
personas.description: You work with APIs or middleware and want broader expertise in identity and deployment.

personas.label: Technology leaders
personas.description: You want a credential path that can lead toward Technical Architect (CTA).

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the System Architect path?
examDifficulty.summary: System Architect has no stand-alone exam. Salesforce awards it once you hold four certifications: Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect. The challenge is preparing across development, integration, identity, and release management.
bullets: No separate System Architect exam. The credential is granted when all four required certifications are active.
Four exams in the path. Complete Platform Developer I and the three architect exams.
Broad subject coverage. Study integration, OAuth and SSO, sandbox planning, and release management.
Check each exam guide. Each certification has its own format, passing score, and fee.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Many candidates complete Platform Developer I first, then schedule the architect exams in an order that fits their experience. Plan and practise for each exam on its own.

examFormat.heading: How the System Architect credential works
examFormat.intro: There is no exam to book specifically for System Architect. You earn the credential by completing four certifications:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Each exam includes short business scenarios. You may need to choose an identity setup for a partner portal or an approach for a scheduled data transfer.
bestWayToPass: Start with Platform Developer I: Build the Apex and data-model knowledge used by the architect exams.
Study integration patterns: Integration Architect covers APIs, error handling, and integration choices.
Learn identity and access management: Review SAML, OAuth, My Domain, and user provisioning.
Prepare for deployment and lifecycle topics: Study sandboxes, source control, testing, and releases.

certificationCard.description: System Architect is a credential earned by completing four certifications: Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect. There is no separate System Architect exam. Platform Developer I also counts toward Application Architect, so the two paths share one exam.

keyConcepts.h2: System Architect: areas covered by the credentials

blocks.heading: Select the right integration pattern
blocks.body: Integration Architect scenarios often turn on whether a user waits for a response, how much data moves, and which system starts the exchange. Use a request-and-reply approach when a user needs an immediate answer. Use asynchronous events or outbound messages when no immediate response is required. Bulk API supports large data loads. Salesforce Connect can expose remote data without copying it into Salesforce. Also understand callout limits: up to 100 callouts per transaction and 120 seconds total.

blocks.heading: Match OAuth flows to the client
blocks.body: Identity and Access Management covers OAuth flows. The web server flow suits a user signing in through a browser when the app server can protect a secret. The user-agent flow serves browser or mobile apps. JWT bearer supports server-to-server access without an interactive user. Device flow fits devices with limited input, such as a TV or command-line client. Refresh tokens let an app obtain new access tokens without prompting the user each time. Connected Apps and External Client Apps define scopes and policies.

blocks.heading: Use APIs and middleware to simplify integrations
blocks.body: As the number of connected systems grows, direct point-to-point links become difficult to maintain. MuleSoft’s API-led model uses System APIs to connect to back-end systems, Process APIs to combine data and apply rules, and Experience APIs to tailor data for an app or channel. Reusable APIs reduce duplicate connections. In Salesforce, Named Credentials store endpoint and authentication details so secrets are not embedded in Apex.

blocks.heading: Plan sandbox and release processes
blocks.body: Use Developer sandboxes for individual work, Partial Copy sandboxes for QA, and Full sandboxes for performance or final user testing. Track metadata in Git and deploy with Salesforce CLI or DevOps Center. Apex deployments to production require at least 75% overall test coverage, and each trigger must be covered. Validate before release and use quick deploy within the permitted 10-day window. Salesforce has no rollback button, so preserve a known-good version and consider feature flags.

blocks.heading: Configure SSO and identity
blocks.body: Single sign-on lets employees use an existing company identity provider. With SAML, a service such as Okta or Entra ID authenticates the person and Salesforce acts as the service provider. Salesforce can also act as an identity provider for other apps. My Domain supplies the organization-specific login URL needed for SSO. Just-in-time provisioning creates or updates a Salesforce user at first SSO login. Experience Cloud can also support customer social sign-on and self-registration.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare across the System Architect exams
scenarioTips.intro: The credential requires four exams, so plan study and practice for each certification. These themes recur across the path.

blocks.heading: Choose an integration pattern
blocks.body: Use synchronous calls when the user needs a response, asynchronous methods when they do not, Bulk API for large transfers, and Salesforce Connect when data should remain remote.

blocks.heading: Plan data migration
blocks.body: Load parent records before child records, use external IDs for relationships, limit unnecessary automation during the load, and use Bulk API for large volumes.

blocks.heading: Decide whether to use one or several orgs
blocks.body: One org is usually simpler. Separate orgs may be justified by legal separation or very different business needs, but they then require integrations.

blocks.heading: Design for platform limits
blocks.body: Make processing bulk-safe. Move lengthy work to Queueable or Batch Apex and use selective queries on large datasets.

blocks.heading: Expose remote data when needed
blocks.body: Salesforce Connect and external objects fit data that changes often and should not be stored in Salesforce.

nextCertsAfter.intro: Once you hold System Architect and Application Architect, the next step is Technical Architect (CTA):

sampleQuestions.question: Which certifications are required to earn System Architect?
options: Pass a single System Architect exam
Pass Platform Developer I and the three System Architect architect exams
Pass Administrator, Platform App Builder, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect
Pass Administrator, Advanced Administrator, and Platform Developer II
sampleQuestions.explanation: System Architect is awarded when the candidate holds Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect.
whyWrong: There is no stand-alone System Architect exam.
That list is the Application Architect path, not System Architect.
Those exams do not make up a Salesforce architect credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A partner’s scheduled backend service must call Salesforce APIs without prompting an employee to sign in. Which OAuth flow should the integration use?
options: Device flow
Web server flow
JWT bearer flow
User-agent flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: JWT bearer lets the partner service authenticate as a configured integration identity using a signed assertion rather than an interactive login.
whyWrong: Device flow is designed for devices with limited input and includes user authorization.
Web server flow requires a user to sign in through a browser.
User-agent flow is intended for a browser or mobile app with a user present.

sampleQuestions.question: Employees use Okta to sign in to company applications and should use it for Salesforce too. Which roles do the systems play?
options: Both systems are identity providers
Salesforce is the identity provider and Okta is the service provider
Okta is the identity provider and Salesforce is the service provider
Neither; this setup uses OAuth only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Okta authenticates the employee as the identity provider. Salesforce is the service provider the employee wants to access.
whyWrong: In this arrangement, Okta is the identity provider and Salesforce is the service provider.
This reverses the roles: Okta handles authentication and Salesforce receives it.
Employee SSO commonly uses SAML; OAuth serves a different access-granting purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: A new employee should receive a Salesforce user account during their first SSO login. What feature supports this?
options: A login flow
Just-in-time provisioning
Delegated authentication
A permission set group
sampleQuestions.explanation: Just-in-time provisioning uses identity information in the SAML assertion to create or update a user on first login.
whyWrong: Login flows add steps after authentication; they do not create the user account.
Delegated authentication checks credentials against another system but does not provision users.
Permission set groups grant permissions to users who already exist.

sampleQuestions.question: A migration must load three million Contacts related to 400,000 Accounts. Which order and method should the architect use?
options: Load records one by one through REST API
Enter the data manually in separate batches
Load Contacts before the related Accounts
Load Accounts first; link each Contact by external ID
sampleQuestions.explanation: Load parent Accounts first, then Contacts. External IDs support the relationships, and Bulk API handles the large volume.
whyWrong: Millions of individual calls would be slow and may hit API limits.
Manual entry is not practical at this scale.
The parent Accounts must exist before Contacts can reference them.

sampleQuestions.question: Two business units have very different processes and regulations require their customer records to be fully separated. What architecture is appropriate?
options: One org with different record types
One org with separate apps in the App Launcher
One org with different page layouts
Separate orgs for the business units
sampleQuestions.explanation: A legal requirement for data separation can justify multiple orgs. The design must also account for integrations between them.
whyWrong: Record types distinguish processes but do not create separate orgs or data stores.
Apps change navigation, not access to data at the org boundary.
Page layouts change the user interface, not data separation.

sampleQuestions.question: What Salesforce feature is required for configuring SAML single sign-on?
options: Shield Platform Encryption
My Domain
Experience Cloud
A Full sandbox
sampleQuestions.explanation: My Domain gives an org its own login URL and is required for SSO configuration.
whyWrong: Encryption is not a prerequisite for setting up SSO.
Experience Cloud supports external sites but is not required for employee SSO.
SSO can be configured without a Full sandbox.

sampleQuestions.question: Service agents need to view warehouse orders that change every few minutes and must remain in the warehouse system. What should the architect choose?
options: A custom Salesforce object refreshed hourly
Salesforce Connect with external objects
A nightly Bulk API data load
Outbound messages from Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce Connect can display live external data without storing a copy in Salesforce.
whyWrong: An hourly copy would be stored and may be stale.
A nightly load stores a copy that can be nearly a day out of date.
Outbound messages send information from Salesforce to another system.

sampleQuestions.question: A trigger must send each new Order to an ERP, where each call takes several seconds. What is a sound design?
options: Queue the callout for asynchronous Apex processing
Require the user to click a send button for every Order
Make a synchronous callout directly from the trigger
Wait for a nightly job to transmit every Order
sampleQuestions.explanation: Queueable Apex can perform the callout asynchronously without making the user wait.
whyWrong: Manual steps can be missed and do not reliably send every Order.
Triggers cannot make synchronous callouts, and synchronous work would delay the user.
A nightly job may delay orders for many hours.

sampleQuestions.question: Five systems need customer data from SAP. Each currently has a separate direct connection, and changes repeatedly break integrations. What should the architect recommend?
options: Create reusable APIs through middleware
Add another direct SAP connection
Copy the SAP data into every system nightly
Stop sharing customer data between systems
sampleQuestions.explanation: A reusable System API in front of SAP reduces duplicate connections and means an SAP change can be handled centrally.
whyWrong: A new direct connection increases the number of integrations to maintain.
Nightly copies can be stale and still require separate integrations.
The business still needs the data, so removing access does not meet the need.

sampleQuestions.question: What Apex test coverage is required for production deployment?
options: Tests are needed only for managed packages
No tests are required
Every Apex class must have exactly 100% coverage
At least 75% overall coverage, with every trigger covered
sampleQuestions.explanation: Apex in a production deployment needs at least 75% overall coverage, and each trigger must be covered.
whyWrong: All Apex deployed to production is subject to test requirements.
Apex tests are required.
One hundred percent is a useful goal but not the minimum rule.

sampleQuestions.question: The team wants to validate a deployment on Monday and release quickly during a short window on Wednesday. What should it do?
options: Validate Monday, then quick deploy Wednesday
Upload a new change set during Wednesday’s window
Deploy Monday and roll back if there is a problem
Wait to run all tests on Wednesday
sampleQuestions.explanation: A validated deployment can be quick deployed within 10 days without rerunning tests.
whyWrong: A new deployment would require tests during the short window.
Salesforce does not provide a general rollback button.
Running tests during the window takes longer than a quick deploy.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer mobile app must access Salesforce as the signed-in customer and keep the session usable for weeks. What should it use?
options: An API key embedded in the mobile app
The username-password OAuth flow
An OAuth flow with a refresh token
One shared integration user for every customer
sampleQuestions.explanation: A refresh token lets the app obtain new access tokens without repeatedly asking the customer to sign in, while preserving the customer identity.
whyWrong: A secret embedded in an app can be extracted and is not used this way.
The username-password flow requires handling the customer’s password and is discouraged.
A shared account would hide which customer performed each action.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should Apex retrieve an external endpoint and its authentication details?
options: A Named Credential
A Custom Label
A text field on a custom record
Hard-coded values in the Apex class
sampleQuestions.explanation: Named Credentials securely store the endpoint and authentication configuration for callouts.
whyWrong: Custom Labels are for translated text, not credentials.
A record field could expose the secret to users with access.
Secrets in source code are visible to code readers and require code changes to update.

sampleQuestions.question: What should be the source of truth for Salesforce metadata in a source-driven development process?
options: A shared Full sandbox
Use production as the only copy and track changes in release notes
A version control system such as Git
A spreadsheet of requested changes
sampleQuestions.explanation: Git tracks the metadata history and serves as the source from which orgs are deployed and updated.
whyWrong: Sandboxes can be refreshed and lose work.
Direct production changes are difficult to track and reproduce.
A spreadsheet is not the metadata and can quickly become stale.

sampleQuestions.question: A payroll provider can handle temporary API failures but must never create a duplicate reimbursement. What should the integration include?
options: A fresh request identifier for each retry attempt
An immediate retry for every timeout response
A longer timeout before the first API request
A stable request key with duplicate detection
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusing a stable key lets the receiver recognize a repeated operation even if the earlier response was lost.
whyWrong: A new identifier makes two attempts look like distinct operations.
Immediate retries can increase load and still create a duplicate.
A longer timeout cannot prove whether an operation was applied.

sampleQuestions.question: Two people change the same Salesforce flow in separate feature branches. When should the team resolve the overlap?
options: After both branches have been deployed to production
When retrieving the resulting metadata from production
When refreshing the developer sandboxes after the release
While merging and validating the changes in version control
sampleQuestions.explanation: Resolve the flow change in source, then validate the combined configuration before promoting it.
whyWrong: Each deployment can overwrite part of the other change.
Retrieving metadata later does not prevent a production regression.
A sandbox refresh propagates the released state without resolving the original conflict.

sampleQuestions.question: External staff use SSO. Removing an employee in the identity provider must also remove their Salesforce access. What should be designed?
options: A deprovisioning integration with account and session controls
A login page with a generic error for inactive staff
Just-in-time provisioning for new employee sign-ins
A second login policy in each employee’s browser
sampleQuestions.explanation: Deprovisioning handles account removal and active Salesforce sessions as well as future sign-ins.
whyWrong: A login error does not revoke active access.
Just-in-time provisioning creates accounts at login.
A browser policy cannot reliably manage a Salesforce account or sessions.

sampleQuestions.question: An inbound status update can arrive before the corresponding order reaches Salesforce. How should the integration handle the race?
options: Insert a new order record for each incoming status update
Buffer the status and replay it after the order is created
Discard the status whenever its order is missing
Ask the source to turn off all asynchronous status events
sampleQuestions.explanation: A durable buffer preserves the update and allows it to be reconciled using the order’s external identifier.
whyWrong: Creating orders from every status can duplicate the source order.
Discarding statuses can leave orders in an incorrect state.
Synchronous delivery alone would not guarantee correct timing.

sampleQuestions.question: An Apex deployment is valid, but the release introduces a new configuration that support must turn off quickly if needed. What should the design include?
options: A manual edit to the installed Apex code
A sandbox refresh during the release window
A configuration flag tested in both states
A higher coverage target for the existing tests
sampleQuestions.explanation: A tested flag gives support a way to disable the new behavior without a code deployment.
whyWrong: Editing deployed code is slower and creates source drift.
Refreshing a sandbox does not change released behavior.
A coverage target does not provide an operational control.
